{
  "summary": "Enforces protocol bounds on outbound P2P messages in CConnman::PushMessage() using an Assume() assertion. Oversized message types (longer than 12 bytes) and payloads exceeding the 4 MB limit are dropped and logged in release builds or asserted in debug builds. The sendmsgtopeer RPC is also updated to reject oversized payloads before queuing.",
  "problem": "Outbound message serialization relies on message types fitting within a 12-byte field and payloads staying under 4 MB, but CConnman did not validate these invariants before queuing messages. Oversized message types cause V1 transport encoding to abort, while V2 transport can overwrite payload bytes or write out of bounds. Oversized payloads could also be queued by internal callers or testing RPCs, violating protocol limits.",
  "evidence": [
    "Commit 4b10305dee and the PR description note: 'Outbound transports encode message types in a fixed 12-byte wire field. V1 aborts on a longer type, while V2 can overwrite the first payload byte or write past its encoding buffer.'",
    "Commit f9188114c7 notes: 'Treat an oversized payload from an internal caller as a failed assumption in CConnman::PushMessage() before it enters the send queue.'"

result.card: Adds bounds checking for outbound message types and payload sizes in CConnman::PushMessage(). Previously, queuing an oversized message type could abort V1 encoding or cause buffer overwrites in V2 transport, and oversized payloads violated the 4 MB protocol limit. The change drops invalid messages in release builds via Assume() assertions and enforces the 4 MB payload limit in the sendmsgtopeer RPC. It has no open PR dependencies.
